comment: Per-service scope for the What's New ingest (src/ingest/docs-whats-new.ts) and, downstream, check-coverage.ts's actionability filter. Two things are decided here, deliberately kept apart from code so they can be revised without touching the ingest or the detector: (1) which services this deck watches for news at all — the global feed carries every AWS service, and only the ones listed here are pulled out of it; (2) how deep the deck's coverage promise goes for each — 'comprehensive' means a matched, uncovered entry is a real gap (the deck claims to track this service's news); 'boundary' means the deck deliberately covers only a narrow question about the service (Quick vs. Kiro), so a feature-level announcement outside that question is real news but not a gap in what this deck promises. Matching is substring, case-insensitive, against the announcement title + permalink — the same crude-but-auditable approach the coverage detector already uses for card-subject matching, chosen for the same reason: a keyword list is a diff a human can review, an embedding match is not.

services.note: Already watched via agentcore.release-notes; kept here too so a What's New item that release-notes' devguide page misses (a cross-cutting announcement, say) is not silently lost.

Bedrock's own document-history page fails the coverage admission test (too much doc-reorg noise — see check-coverage.ts's NEWS_KINDS comment). This is the source that actually lets Bedrock product news reach the detector.
Strands has no curated changelog (see docs-release-notes.ts and the excluded github-releases source); AWS's own What's New posts about Strands are the one curated, dated surface available.

The deck covers Quick only for the business-vs-engineer boundary question (README: 'the Quick business-vs-engineer boundary'), not Quick's feature roadmap. A feature GA (new connector, new extension) is real Quick news but not a gap in this deck's stated scope unless it topically bears on the boundary question itself.

First addition under the 2026-08-20 scope widening (docs/decisions/2026-08-20-scope-widened-to-aws-ai-broadly.md), added deliberately one service at a time rather than all at once. Depth is 'boundary', not 'comprehensive', on purpose: measured 8 of one feed page's SageMaker entries as JumpStart model-roster additions (downweighted to 'minor' in coverage.ts's JUMPSTART_MODEL_RE, same anti-pattern as Bedrock's model roster), so genuine platform-feature volume through this filter is still unproven. Revisit depth once a few real cycles show what actually reaches the actionable queue.
